topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the lecture series, and the learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer development.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetic, Endogenous, and Epidemiological Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational causes of cancer, comparing intrinsic genetic mutations and bad luck with inherited predispositions and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Examples of Environmental and Biological Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific carcinogenic exposures—including pathogens, dietary toxins, radiation, and industrial chemicals—and their mechanisms as tumor initiators or promoters across different tissues and life stages.

topics.label: Methods for Determining Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the analytical and experimental methods used to identify carcinogens—such as mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, animal models, and the Ames test—and conclude with risk-benefit considerations.
